note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 19, 16; A06b Const 19, 16; L05 Const 24(1); Const 24(4)): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Wedlock restriction), A01b (descent, born abroad: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A02a (birth in country: Parental residence restriction) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a wedlock restriction (a child born out of wedlock may not take it from a citizen father), which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Federal Constitution, Reprint as at 15 October 2020 (Attorney General's Chambers, Laws of Malaysia online), Art. 19(1), (3); Federal Constitution, Art. 24(1) and Second Schedule Part II s. 1; Constitution (Amendment) Act 2025, Act A1752 (Royal Assent 7 March 2025, gazetted 20 March 2025), ss. 1(2), 11(a)(i). It confirmed the years of residence, renunciation, loss on taking another citizenship, birth in the territory, birth in the territory's condition, descent and the limit abroad. The naturalisation oath (First Schedule) wasn't read, so renunciation rests on the dataset. The Constitution (Amendment) Act 2025, Act A1752, would end birthplace citizenship for a child of a permanent resident and let a citizen mother pass citizenship abroad, but comes into operation on a date to be appointed by Gazette notification, which wasn't found: it is recorded here, not held.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Malaysia, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Malaysia for 12 months immediately prior to the application, and was resident (holding Malaysian permanent resident status) in the country for 10 out of 12 years prior to the application. ... n.a. ... Person acquired citizenship of another country by a voluntary and formal act other than by marriage; Person is a woman who is a citizen by registration and who subsequently acquired citizenship of another country through marriage with a foreigner. ... Wedlock restriction ... Person is born in Malaysia to a citizenship mother or in wedlock to a citizen father. ... Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply) ... Person is born abroad to a father who is a citizen and was born in Malaysia, to a father who is a citizen and resident abroad in the service of the government, or to a father who is a citizen and the child is registered with the Malaysian authorities within 1 year after birth.; Person is under the age of 21 years and was born abroad to a mother who is a citizen and a father who is not a citizen. ... Parental residence restriction ... Person is born in Malaysia to a permanently resident foreigner. Unless born to a father who is a foreign diplomat, or the father is an enemy alien and the child is born in a place then under occupation by the enemy. ... No provision

sources.title: Federal Constitution, Reprint as at 15 October 2020 (Attorney General's Chambers, Laws of Malaysia online), Art. 19(1), (3)
sources.said: 19. (1) Subject to Clause (9), the Federal Government may, upon application made by any person of or over the age of twenty-one years who is not a citizen, grant a certificate of naturalization to that person if satisfied— (a) that— (i) he has resided in the Federation for the required periods and intends, if the certificate is granted, to do so permanently; ... (3) The periods of residence in the Federation or the relevant part of it which are required for the grant of a certificate of naturalization are periods which amount in the aggregate to not less than ten years in the twelve years immediately preceding the date of the application for the certificate, and which include the twelve months immediately preceding that date.

sources.title: Federal Constitution, Art. 24(1) and Second Schedule Part II s. 1
sources.said: 24. (1) If the Federal Government is satisfied that any citizen has acquired by registration, naturalization or other voluntary and formal act (other than marriage) the citizenship of any country outside the Federation, the Federal Government may by order deprive that person of his citizenship. ... 1. ... (a) every person born within the Federation of whose parents one at least is at the time of the birth either a citizen or permanently resident in the Federation; and (b) every person born outside the Federation whose father is at the time of the birth a citizen and either was born in the Federation or is at the time of the birth in the service of the Federation or of a State; and (c) every person born outside the Federation whose father is at the time of the birth a citizen and whose birth is, within one year of its occurrence ... registered at a consulate of the Federation

sources.title: Constitution (Amendment) Act 2025, Act A1752 (Royal Assent 7 March 2025, gazetted 20 March 2025), ss. 1(2), 11(a)(i)
sources.said: (2) This Act comes into operation on a date to be appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong by notification in the Gazette ... 11. The Second Schedule to the Federal Constitution is amended— (a) in Part II— (i) in section 1— (A) in paragraph (a), by substituting for the words “either a citizen or permanently resident in the Federation” the words “a citizen”; (B) in paragraph (b)— (AA) by substituting for the words “whose father” the words “of whose parents one at least”

atBirth.soilIf: Person is born in Malaysia to a permanently resident foreigner. Unless born to a father who is a foreign diplomat, or the father is an enemy alien and the child is born in a place then under occupation by the enemy.
atBirth.descentAbroad: Person is born abroad to a father who is a citizen and was born in Malaysia, to a father who is a citizen and resident abroad in the service of the government, or to a father who is a citizen and the child is registered with the Malaysian authorities within 1 year after birth.; Person is under the age of 21 years and was born abroad to a mother who is a citizen and a father who is not a citizen.
